title: Handoffs & the Task Board
objective: After this lesson you will be able to run a shared task board (open/claimed/done/skipped with single ownership), enforce handoff contracts between agents, and detect dropped/duplicated work from board state alone.
why: Agents sharing nothing duplicate work; sharing everything collide. The task board is the collaboration contract made visible: who owns what, what's done, what was skipped and why. Every 'two agents emailed the customer' and 'nobody validated the amount' incident is a board-design failure — ownership states prevent both by construction.

blocks.text: Ownership states: open, claimed, done, skipped

Every task carries **owner + state**: `open` (unassigned), `claimed` (exactly one agent working), `done` (with output reference), `skipped` (with reason, never silent). Claim-before-work prevents duplication (two agents see claimed, only owner proceeds); completion receipts prevent drops (unclaimed + undone at shift-end is visible backlog, not mystery).

blocks.caption: Ownership in code: races resolved, skips reasoned, backlog visible

blocks.text: Agent-to-agent transfers carry the Ch.3 task contract plus board mechanics: producer marks done *with output reference*, consumer claims *with input validation* (re-validate received shapes — trust boundaries exist between agents too). Failed validation routes to rework (same producer, quoted defect) not forward — defects caught at transfer cost one step; downstream, they cost the run.
Reading the board: drops vs dupes

Board state diagnoses team health at a glance: growing `open` + idle agents = routing failure (work unassigned); same task `claimed` twice-attempted = race handling working (second claim refused — by design); `done` without outputRef = protocol violation (completion theater); `skipped` without reason = audit hole. Review boards like logs: patterns, not entries.

blocks.title: Work the board
blocks.note: Run it: expect true, false, false, true — first claim wins, second refused (race handled), wrong-owner completion refused, owner completes. Ownership enforced in code, not hoped in prompts.

items: Board states (open/claimed/done/skipped) with exactly-one-owner enforced in code
Handoffs contracted + consumer-validated; defects route to rework with quoted defects
Board patterns diagnose health: unclaimed backlog, refused races (good), theater completions, reasonless skips

exercise.prompt: (a) Run the practice board and map each boolean to its rule. (b) Extend with skip(id, agent, reason) enforcing reason presence + owner-or-open rule, plus a backlog() listing unfinished ids; test all paths. (c) State what 'done without outputRef' and 'skipped without reason' each indicate about team health.
hints: Mapping: first-claim wins / race refused / non-owner completion refused / owner completes — four rules, four lines.
skip: reason required (empty → refuse); owner-or-open else refuse; backlog: open + claimed ids (claimed-and-stalled needs heartbeat extension in production — note it).
done-without-ref = completion theater (unverifiable claims); skip-without-reason = audit hole (unreviewable omission).
exercise.why: Ownership mechanics (claim races, completion rights, reasoned skips) plus health reading (patterns as diagnostics) are the collaboration contract made executable — practiced in code, not described in prose.
exercise.code: // Board-extension pattern: state machine + rights checks + tests per path.

quiz.q: Two agents email one customer. Board-level root cause?
options: No claimed ownership: unowned shared work duplicates — claim-before-work with exactly-one-owner prevents it
quiz.explain: Without ownership states, shared work forks. First-claim-wins plus completion rights make duplication structurally impossible.

quiz.q: Second claim on a claimed task is refused. Correct?
options: Correct by design: races resolve to first-claimer; refusal is the mechanism working, logged for audit
quiz.explain: Refused second claims prove the race handler works. Log them (contention signal) but never bypass ownership.

options: Completion theater: unverifiable claims — done requires outputRef, enforced in code
quiz.explain: Outputs need references for downstream consumption and audit. Ref-less done is a claim without evidence — code must refuse it.

summary: Boards with enforced ownership (claim/complete/skip + reasons), contracted validated handoffs, and pattern-level health reading. Collaboration by construction, not hope.
